articles.title: New software package: ERPLAB Studio
articles.content:
We are excited to announce the release of a new EEG/ERP analysis package, ERPLAB Studio. We think it’s a huge improvement over the classic EEGLAB user interface. See our cheesy “advertisement” video to get a quick overview.

Rather than operating as an EEGLAB plugin, ERPLAB Studio is a standalone Matlab program that provides a more efficient and user-friendly interface to the most commonly used EEGLAB and ERPLAB routines.

With ERPLAB Studio, you automatically see the EEG or ERP waveforms as soon as you load a file. And as soon as you perform an operation, you see what the new EEG/ERP looks like. For example, when you filter the data, you immediately see the filtered waveforms.

You can even select multiple datasets and apply an operation like artifact detection on all of them in one step. And then you can immediately see the results, such as which EEG epochs have been marked with artifacts.

We give you access to EEGLAB’s ICA-based artifact correction tools, but with a nice bonus. You can plot the ICA activations in the same window with the EEG data, making it easy to see which ICA components correspond to specific artifacts such as eyeblinks.

The program has an EEG tab for processing continuous and epoched EEG data, and an ERP tab for processing averaged ERPs.

The automatic ERP plotting makes it easy for you to view the data laid out according to the electrode locations. And we have an Advanced Waveform Viewer that can make publication-quality plots.

ERPLAB Studio is mainly just a new user interface. Under the hood, we’re running the same EEGLAB and ERPLAB routines you’ve always used. And scripting is identical.

ERPLAB Studio is included in version 11 and higher of ERPLAB. You simply follow our download/installation instructions and then type estudio from the Matlab command line.

If you’re new to ERPLAB, we strongly recommend that you go through our tutorial before starting to process your own data.

If you already know how to use the original version of ERPLAB (which we now call ERPLAB Classic), you can quickly learn how to use ERPLAB Studio with our Transition Guide.

We also have a manual that describes every feature in detail.

articles.content: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an increasingly popular neuroimaging technique that measures cortical hemodynamic activity in a non-invasive and portable fashion. articles.content: Recent technological developments have brought optically pumped magnetometers (OPMs) within reach of the larger neuroscientific community. The current state-of-the-art consists of whole-head systems that measure the magnetic field at >100 locations. OPM sensors can be constructed to measure the field in either 1, 2, or 3 orientations. articles.content: The choices we make during the recording, preprocessing and analysis of event-related potentials (ERP) data can affect study outcomes. As such, it is critical that they are transparently reported to allow for reproducibility. articles.content: The Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) is a widely adopted, community-driven standard to organize neuroimaging data and metadata. Although numerous extensions have been developed to incrementally extend coverage to new modalities and data types, an unambiguous, granular specification for eye-tracking recordings is lacking. Here, we present how BIDS will structure data and metadata produced by eye-tracking devices, including gaze position and pupil data. In addition to prescribing the...

articles.title: Facilitating unusual bodily experiences and out-of-body experiences across wakefulness and sleep: A high-density EEG and neurophenomenology study
articles.content: Unusual bodily experiences (UBEs) are illusory bodily perceptions that are not coherent with typical wakeful experiences, including flying or floating sensations, body distortions, and out-of-body experiences. This study examines UBEs in a controlled sleep laboratory using meditation and light stimulation to facilitate their occurrence. A total of N = 35 healthy participants underwent high-density EEG, with additional EMG, EOG, and ECG recordings. Participants signalled UBEs by performing...

articles.title: The Impact of Brain Tumors and Craniotomy Lesions on Scalp EEG
articles.content: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in both research and clinical settings, yet its accuracy can be significantly impacted by subject-specific anatomical anomalies such as brain lesions and skull defects. This study investigates the effects of glioma-related brain lesions and craniotomy-induced bone discontinuities on scalp-recorded EEG signals. To do this, single- and multi-source simulations were created using individualized forward models with and without these structural anomalies....

articles.title: EMG-BIDS: an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure for electromyography
articles.content: Electromyography (EMG) is fundamental to clinical assessment, rehabilitation, neuromuscular research, and human-machine interfaces. Despite decades of use, no widely adopted standard exists for organizing and sharing EMG data, limiting reusability and large-scale data aggregation. We present EMG-BIDS, an extension to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) that standardizes the organization of EMG recordings. articles.title: Screening-based prevalence and axis distribution of astigmatism among children and adolescents in Lintong District, Xi'an: a large-scale school-based cross-sectional study
articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: Astigmatism was common in this large district school screening dataset and differed by school stage, axis type, and refractive-status category. The findings may help local screening programs plan re-examination and referral pathways, but they should not be interpreted as cycloplegic clinical diagnoses or as evidence of temporal progression or causality.

articles.title: Clinical profiles, referral patterns and low vision aid prescribing across four rehabilitation centres in Ghana: protocol for a multicentre retrospective record review
articles.content: BACKGROUND: Low vision, defined as best-corrected visual acuity of less than 6/18 in the better eye or a visual field constriction of 20° or less, is a condition in which residual vision may be optimized through optical and non-optical aids. Despite the importance of low vision services in maximizing residual vision and supporting rehabilitation and quality of life, evidence on patient profiles and service delivery in Ghana remains limited. The HM KNUST Low Vision Project aims to address this...
articles.author: Werner Eisenbarth

articles.title: Tele-optometry for eye disease screening: a scoping review of context-dependent diagnostic performance and limitations for large-scale implementation
articles.content: CONCLUSION: Tele-diagnostic screening shows promise for high-prevalence conditions with straightforward criteria, such as DR and refractive error, but is less reliable for complex diseases like glaucoma. These conclusions are constrained by limited downstream-outcome reporting and geographic concentration. Policymakers should prioritize validated applications and avoid premature scale-up to safeguard patient safety.
articles.author: Chigozie Ekenze

articles.title: Early changes in the central vision and the macula in diabetic retinal disease: associations with serum biomarkers
articles.content: CONCLUSION: This study links subtle macular neural and vascular changes with systemic biomarkers in diabetic patients without visible macular lesions. Impaired central vision was associated with shorter PROS, lower RPE volume, and reduced vascular parameters. These findings improve understanding of early DRD and suggest that monitoring HbA1c, HDL, oxidized LDL, uric acid, and hsCRP may help estimate the risk of visual impairment.

articles.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study
articles.content: CONCLUSION: Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.
articles.author: Sunjin Hwang

articles.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus
articles.content: CONCLUSIONS: At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

articles.title: From task-specific AI to multimodal foundation models in PET/CT: a readiness framework for clinical translation
articles.content: Artificial intelligence in PET/CT is evolving from narrowly optimized systems toward reusable pretrained representations and multimodal models.
